briefing.text: Under this benchmark's convention, a hypothesis that names this study's cancer type and genes/variants is about this study and is labelled True or False even if the tables lack a direct pathway readout (no expression, phospho-ERK or functional data). First check whether the cohort is iCCA (CANCER_TYPE / ONCOTREE codes in data_clinical_sample.txt) and whether ARAF N217I and G322S appear in data_mutations.txt. If both hold, decide between True and False using the closest variables plus established biology, and do not choose 'Not verifiable' just because there is no readout.
briefing.reason: The likeliest mistake here is choosing 'Not verifiable' because no pathway-activity variable exists. That choice is graded wrong if the hypothesis comes from this study.

briefing.text: The cohort is very small (about 8 WXS samples, with few ARAF-mutant cases). Any significance test will have almost no power, so a non-significant result is not evidence against the hypothesis. Do not base a False label on a lack of significance.
briefing.reason: Stops the team from reading underpowered tests as a contradiction.

briefing.text: Mutual exclusivity is a descriptive, indirect check of the pathway. For each sample, tabulate the MAPK-pathway drivers (KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, ARAF, ERBB2, and FGFR2 fusions in data_sv.txt), plus IDH1/2. Then check whether the ARAF-mutant samples carry or lack other MAPK drivers. Lacking them fits ARAF being the pathway driver. Having a strong co-driver weakens that case. Report this only descriptively, since n is tiny.
briefing.reason: This is the closest test in the data itself of whether ARAF mutations act as pathway drivers.

briefing.text: Map ARAF Protein_position 217 and 322 (canonical transcript NM_001654, 606 aa) onto the domains. Residue 217 sits near the CR2 regulatory region, which includes the 14-3-3 binding site around S214 (analogous to RAF1 S259 and BRAF S365). Mutations at that site are a known mechanism of RAF activation (e.g. ARAF S214 in lung cancer, RAF1 S257/S259 in Noonan syndrome). Residue 322 is near the start of the kinase domain. Weigh this domain context when using established biology.
briefing.reason: With no functional readout, the domain locations are the main biological evidence the team can bring to bear.

briefing.text: If the MAF shows Hotspot=0 for a variant, or the variant is missing from known catalogues, that is not evidence it is non-functional. Discovery studies often test novel variants in experiments whose results are not deposited in cBioPortal tables. The deposited files here are only the MAF, SV, gene panel and clinical tables.
briefing.reason: Stops the team from reading the hotspot annotation as evidence against activation.

briefing.text: ARAF is on chromosome X. Check that the ARAF calls are somatic (Mutation_Status, matched normal) and whether t_alt_count/n_alt_count are populated. If the read counts are empty, VAF cannot be assessed, so note that limitation and rely on the study's somatic calling instead of discarding the calls.
briefing.reason: This is a quality check on the variant calls the hypothesis depends on, and it covers what to do if VAF cannot be computed.

shared_assumptions: Both teams treated the hypothesis as a single claim and assumed that if ARAF mutations are present in this iCCA study, both named variants (N217I and G322S) activate the pathway; neither team judged each variant on its own.

Both teams assumed the hypothesis is the study's finding stated as reported. Neither considered that the benchmark also builds hypotheses by reversing a finding, for example by making a claim about one variant cover both, or by turning a variant with impaired or no activity into an activating one.
Both teams took 'no other MAPK driver in ICC12/ICC18' as support for ARAF driving the pathway. Mutual exclusivity in 8 samples says nothing about whether a variant is activating or loss-of-function.
Both teams relied on the study's calling and did not check the ARAF calls themselves: the normal-allele and read-count fields are empty, ARAF is on chrX and the tables have no sex variable.
unused_evidence: data_sv.txt: RIN1 fusions (RIN1-IGLL5 in ICC12, which carries ARAF G322S; RIN1-IGLJ3 in ICC8 and ICC14). RIN1 is a RAS effector, so these samples are not plainly free of other RAS-pathway events. Neither team's co-driver tabulation included it.

data_mutations.txt protein position and codon fields (Protein_position 217 and 322, Codons aAc/aTc and Ggc/Agc). These let each residue be placed on a RAF domain and aligned to its BRAF/CRAF equivalent. Team A mentioned the CR2 site only for one residue, and team B did not map either residue.
Mutations in the two ARAF-mutant samples outside the canonical RAS/RAF/MEK genes, such as other kinases or pathway negative regulators, were not tabulated in full.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and the full mutation lists of ICC12 and ICC18 were not compared with the other samples.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the lack of a pathway readout as their weakest point and settled it by appealing to 'study finding/biology'. Neither said what the study found for each variant separately, or what established biology says about each residue. The weak point was reported, not resolved.
Team A's somatic-status warning (empty Mutation_Status and read counts, Hotspot=0) was logged with 'no change' and never followed up.
Team B checked no pitfalls (empty pitfalls_checked list).
second_readings: Per-variant reading: 'specifically N217I and G322S lead to activation' claims that both variants are activating. If the study's functional work showed one variant activating and the other not (or impaired), the conjunctive claim would be False even though ARAF mutations as a class matter.

Mechanism reading: 'activation of the pathway' could mean the MAPK/ERK pathway specifically. A variant could be oncogenic or recurrent without raising ERK signalling, or could raise it only through dimerisation with another RAF (a kinase-impaired paradox mechanism).
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust. Both teams agree that the hypothesis is about this study, so Not verifiable is unlikely. But both reached True or False by treating 'N217I and G322S' as one activating class, without checking each variant's biology or the chance that the wording is a reversed or over-generalised finding. Agreement here comes from a shared shortcut, not from independent evidence.

questions.why: Mapping each residue to a well-studied paralog position is the most direct way to judge, from biology, each variant's likely effect on pathway activation.

findings.question: How are RAF kinase mutations classified by mechanism (class I/II RAS-independent activating, class III kinase-impaired or dead), and how do residues in the CR2 regulatory region and in the glycine-rich P-loop of the kinase domain usually map onto these classes?
findings.answer: THE WEB DID NOT SETTLE THIS: the research gateway returned HTTP 502/403 on all 4 calls, so no page was read. Answer from established literature knowledge (Yao et al. 2017 Nature convention). Class I: RAS-independent, signal as active monomers (BRAF V600). Class II: RAS-independent constitutive dimers with high or intermediate kinase activity (BRAF K601, L597, G464, most G469 substitutions including G469A/V/R/S, fusions). Class III: kinase-impaired or dead and RAS-dependent; they activate ERK by transactivating CRAF (BRAF D594, G466, N581, G596, G469E). CR2 mutations at or next to the 14-3-3 site (CRAF S257/S259/P261 in Noonan syndrome and cancer, ARAF S214 in lung adenocarcinoma) are activating: they relieve 14-3-3-mediated autoinhibition and are not kinase-impairing. P-loop glycines split: G464 and G469 mostly class II (activating), G466 class III.

findings.question: How are ARAF residue numbers aligned to the equivalent BRAF and CRAF residues (for example, which ARAF residues correspond to the CRAF S259 14-3-3 site and to the BRAF glycine-rich loop G464-G469)?
findings.answer: THE WEB DID NOT SETTLE THIS: the gateway was down and no page was read. Answer from knowledge. ARAF S214 is the CR2 14-3-3 site, equivalent to CRAF S259 and BRAF S365 (ARAF to CRAF offset +45 in CR2). ARAF N217 lies in the same RSTS(214)TP motif, about CRAF N262, three residues past the 14-3-3 phosphoserine. In the kinase domain the offsets are about +39 to CRAF and +147 to BRAF (catalytic lysine ARAF K336 = CRAF K375 = BRAF K483). The ARAF glycine-rich loop is therefore about G317-G322 (GSGSFG), matching CRAF G356-G361 and BRAF G464-G469. ARAF G322 corresponds to BRAF G469, a class II activating position (G469S is reported as activating), not to class III G466 (about ARAF G319). Both N217I and G322S map to paralog positions where mutations are usually activating, which favours the hypothesis. Check the exact numbering against a UniProt alignment (P10398 / P04049 / P15056) if possible.
